name: Dariacore
swing: 0 (mostly straight; the otoMAD/hyperflip groove and its breakdown approximate a triplet feel at 0.33)
summary: An internet microgenre coined by Jane Remover (as 'Leroy') in the early 2020s, also called hyperflip, built from frenetic cut-ups of pop hooks, anime/TV snippets and internet ephemera smashed together at breakcore-adjacent tempos with Jersey Club bounce, breakbeats, hardstyle kicks and dubstep-derived drops. Its real identity lives as much in what gets sampled and how it's chopped as in any drum pattern — sudden full stops, abrupt genre/tempo whiplash and meme-y fake-outs are as central to the sound as any specific kick placement.

sounds.kick: Borrowed wholesale from whichever donor genre is in play at that moment: Jersey Club's 5-kick shape, a plain hardstyle four-on-the-floor, a displaced jungle/breakbeat kick, or a halftime dubstep kick — often switching between them bar to bar rather than settling on one.
sounds.snare: Breakbeat-style drags and doubles, a hardstyle-adjacent clap+snare stack on 2 and 4, or a halftime backbeat on 3 alone, frequently distorted/pitched to match whatever sample is riding over it.
sounds.hats: Dense 16th closed-hat beds and complextro-style stutter-repeats (the same hit machine-gunned at rapid, decreasing velocity) rather than swung garage-style hats.
sounds.percussion: Largely a placeholder role here: real dariacore leans on sound effects (car crashes, sirens, bed squeaks) and vocal/instrumental sample chops that a drum-only pattern library cannot represent; cowbell/tom hits stand in for siren-stab and impact accents where used.
sounds.cymbals: A single crash or none at all; cymbal choice matters far less than the sample edit riding over the drums.

machines: Akai MPC60 / MPC3000 — chop and re-trigger the breakbeat/Jersey-derived kick-snare skeletons
E-mu SP-1200 — 12-bit crunch for the breakbeat/amen-adjacent grooves
Roland TR-909 / TR-808 — hardstyle-adjacent kick and clap/snare layers
Elektron Machinedrum — glitchy stutter-edit percussion for the complextro-derived grooves
Ensoniq ASR-X — sample-chop workflow suited to the plunderphonics/mashcore splice approach
Ableton Live stock devices (Beat Repeat / Redux-style bitcrush, Gated audio) — the actual sample-flip and stutter engine most dariacore producers use
Vengeance/Sample Focus breakcore & Jersey Club one-shot packs — real drum source material
